label: Diagram 21
caption: Diagram 21 Minimum separation distances from combustible material in or near a chimney
description: The diagram shows a grey rectangular wall or structure with a square 'Flue liner' at its centre, drawn with a heavy black border. Labels point to parts around it. At the top, a narrow vertical rectangle crossed by diagonals is labelled 'Combustible material on metal fastening or support', above a dashed rectangle labelled 'Metal fastening or support'. On the left, a horizontal rectangle crossed by diagonals is labelled 'Combustible material'. On the right edge, a narrow vertical rectangle containing a zig-zag line is labelled 'Skirting board, dado rail, picture rail, etc.', and below it a rectangle crossed by diagonals; a second rectangle crossed by diagonals is also shown below the bottom edge of the grey structure, and the label 'Combustible material other than skirting board, dado rail, picture rail, etc.' points to both of these crossed rectangles. Dimensions mark the gaps: 'At least 50mm' from the top of the flue liner to the metal fastening or support, 'At least 200mm' between the left edge of the grey structure and the left of the flue liner, 'At least 200mm' between the bottom of the flue liner and the bottom edge of the grey structure, 'Less than 200mm' between the right of the flue liner and the right edge of the grey structure, and 'At least 40mm' between the right edge of the grey structure and the crossed rectangle on the right.
